name: Low-Poly Diorama
summary: A toy-like autumn miniature world of flat-shaded triangle facets in soft afternoon light, with tilt-shift blur at the screen edges.
description: Every character, prop, collectible and ground tile is a real triangle mesh, projected with a fixed 44° three-quarter orthographic camera and flat-shaded by one warm sun plus a cool-sky / warm-ground ambient. Characters are rigged meshes (thigh + shin with a knee, upper + fore arm, cape, scarf, neck) re-posed for every frame and baked at 16 yaw angles, so walks, breathing, blinks, lunges, hit reactions and facet break-ups all stay in the medium. The ground is a jittered triangle lattice lit from a tiny height field, composed into meadows, single-species groves, ponds with reed shores and winding trodden paths. Soft indigo cast shadows, glowing carved faces and a tilt-shift band make it feel like a photographed tabletop diorama.
bestFor: top-down action games with crowds of units
avoidFor: projects needing hundreds of unique animated models

difficulty.why: Every new asset is a triangle mesh written as coordinates (lathe profiles, boxes, icospheres, leaf blades) and then baked at 16 yaw angles; that is fiddlier than voxels or flat sprites, but very predictable once the primitives and the shared sun are set up.

technique.renderer: Canvas 2D (procedural, no image assets) with a tiny software 3D pipeline: mesh -> yaw -> orthographic 3/4 projection -> flat shading -> painter's sort -> baked sprites
technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites are baked at K = clamp(round(screenHeight/360 * 4)/4, 2, 4) px per world unit (2.5 px/unit at a 900 px tall screen); the ground is baked in 256-unit chunks at up to 3 px/unit (groundResMax 3).
technique.summary: Real triangle meshes built from lathes, boxes, icospheres and folded leaf blades, flat-shaded per face with a fixed sun and pre-rendered into sprite sheets at 16 yaw angles; the ground is a lit, jittered triangle lattice.
technique.linework: No outlines. Each facet is filled and then stroked in its own colour (lineWidth 0.85 sprite px, 0.6 for decals, 0.5 for gems, round joins) only to hide anti-aliasing seams. Silhouettes read through value contrast against the ground, never through ink lines.
technique.shading: Flat per-face Lambert: colour * (SKY*h + GND*(1-h) + SUN*max(0, n.L)) with h = 0.5 + 0.5*nz, SKY [0.47,0.52,0.67], GND [0.52,0.44,0.38], SUN [0.7,0.62,0.45]. Volume comes from facet orientation plus colour by role: tree crowns pick their dark / mid / light tone from the face normal (nz < -0.12 / middle / nz > 0.42), pine tiers go dark skirt -> mid -> light cap, pumpkins alternate rib colours; only ±3 % per-face jitter on top. Emissive faces (carved eyes, windows, cracks) skip lighting.
technique.lighting: One warm sun from upper-left-front, L = normalize(-0.58, 0.3, 0.76) (x right, y towards camera, z up). Additive warm radial glows ('lighter') around glowing faces, lanterns and gems. Cast shadows are the mesh projected along the sun, blurred and tinted indigo #2c3263 (props: #7d86c4, multiplied at 62 %).
technique.texture: None on surfaces. Texture comes from geometry: 24-unit jittered ground triangles whose tone (4 variants per biome) is chosen by a 64-unit noise field so facets cluster into calm patches, plus baked micro-props placed with intent (leaf litter under crowns, tufts on region edges, reeds on shores).

paletteRules: Everything is mid-value and slightly desaturated; the only fully saturated colours are emissive (carved glow, cracks, gems).
The ground stays in a narrow value band (grass #95b16f-#a3bd7d) so characters pop through hue: orange main character, lilac root creatures, white ghosts.
Shadows and vignettes are cool indigo/violet (#2c3263, rgba(60,55,100,.22), rgba(70,62,110,.26)), never pure black or grey.
Each material has exactly 2-4 base colours (e.g. pumpkin #f48a2c / #e27526) – the lighting creates the rest of the ramp.

Autumn tree crowns use 4 warm triads, each ordered by role [mid, shadow side, sunlit top]: maple reds #dc5d43/#cf4d3c/#e6714b, oak oranges #ee8b3a/#e47a31/#f2a046, birch yellows #ecb544/#e3a23c/#f2c35a, poplar rusts #d07a3f/#c4653a/#e09447. The litter under a tree uses its own triad.
No pure white surfaces except impact flashes and sparkle stars; no pure black anywhere (darkest is #161b33 inside ghost eyes).
Water is the only cool large area; keep it mid-value (#6fb4c8 -> #4b8fb4) so it never out-shouts the orange main character.

typography.role: Headings, HUD counters, floating numbers, big titles
typography.css: font: 800 58px/1 'Baloo 2', 'Nunito', system-ui, sans-serif; color: #fff; letter-spacing: 1px; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 #f39a52, 0 2px 0 #ee8c45, 0 3px 0 #e8803c, 0 4px 0 #e07434, 0 5px 0 #d6692e, 0 12px 20px rgba(60,40,100,.45);

world.summary: An endless faceted tabletop: a jittered triangle lattice (cell 24 world units) whose vertices carry a biome id and a tiny height; each triangle is flat-shaded from its height-field normal with the same sun as the models. Regions are composed, not sprinkled: meadows with flower patches, autumn forests made of single-species groves, rock outcrops, ploughed fields, farm yards, ponds with sand shores, reeds and lily pads, and thin trodden-earth paths that wind through meadows and woods. Decals and prop shadows are baked into 256-unit chunks.
layers: Triangle lattice: CS = 24, row height 24*0.866, vertex jitter ±26 % x / ±23 % y, odd rows offset half a cell

Per-vertex biome, in priority order: rock (fbm/330 > 0.675), field rectangles, pond (fbm/300 > 0.70) with a sand shore band (> 0.684), path (|perlin/560| < 0.042), forest (warped fbm/780 > 0.578), sand, grass; the start area is kept dry
Height = biome base + roughness * (hash * 1.3 + perlin(x/75) * 1.6) + 6 * perlin(x/280); water is flat at -3.0 (roughness 0.14) so the shore facets tilt into a lit bank

Per-facet tone: one of 4 biome variants picked by a 64-unit noise field (+30 % hash), so tones form soft patches; accents 18 % mossy rock #98aa78, 3.5 % dry grass, 6 % darker forest; water deepens towards #4b8fb4 with distance into the pond, rim facets mix 42 % foam #cdeae6
Field biome: furrow ridges every 14 units (3.2-unit darker north band, 3.4-unit lighter south band) with two-tone vine triangles

Decals with intent: 14 crown-coloured leaf triangles in an ellipse under every deciduous tree (shifted to its shadow side), mushrooms at the foot of some pines, tufts and pebbles around boulders and along region edges, flower clusters only inside meadow patches (fbm/110 > 0.6, one colour per patch), reeds on shores, lily pads in pond interiors, pebbles along path edges; a sparse base (about 1 %) everywhere else
Prop shadows baked into the chunk with multiply at alpha 0.62, colour #7d86c4

characters.summary: Chunky toy figures built from lathes (5-16 segments), boxes, 20-face icospheres and folded leaf blades. The main character (~17 x 31 units, scaled 1.1x) is a real rig: ribbed pumpkin head (radius 7.8, ~60 % of the height) with a carved glowing face on a neck pivot, linen shirt #f3e6c8 with a belt buckle, red scarf #d65d42 whose tail hangs from a pivot, a three-ring blue half-cape #4b68a3 whose hem flares, lifts and sways, arms with elbows and legs with knees. 16 baked poses: 8 walk, 4 breathing idle, 1 blink, dash crouch, dash lunge, hurt. Creatures: lilac-and-cream root creatures in two designed variants (round with a four-leaf crown and grin, or tall with a fanned three-blade crest, lopsided fanged grin and a long root tail), a pale teardrop spirit with mitten hands, a trailing wisp and a whipping tail (alpha 0.84), and a purple rock colossus with glowing orange cracks at ~3x the main character.
rules: Head-to-body ratio about 1:1 on the main character – the head is the silhouette; keep it the largest and most saturated shape.
Every character has a glowing or high-contrast face on the +x (front) side so facing reads at 16 directions; faces are flat polygons projected onto the head and stacked rim / fill / hot core.

Build characters as rigs: parts are separate meshes on pivots (hip, knee, shoulder, elbow, neck, cape rings, scarf knot) and every frame is a re-posed mesh baked at 16 yaws – never squash a sprite to fake a pose.
The hip height comes from the stance leg (max over legs of 3.8 cos a + 3.9 cos(a + knee)), so a foot always touches the ground and the bob falls out of the leg pose.
Each creature type has 6 walk poses + 1 hit pose; the small creature comes in 2 designed variants chosen by its seed, not random scale/hue jitter.

Creatures must differ by hue and silhouette: lilac/cream root creatures (round crown or tall crest), pale spirit (teardrop + tail + wisp, ramp #a6b5ec -> #eaf5ff), purple rock colossus (3x size, bands #c19c64 -> #9c7c90 -> #7f5c95, cracks #ffa63a).
Never use ground hues on characters; small creatures stay 16-21 units tall.

props.summary: Scenery is baked once at a single yaw with the same camera, sun and flat shading as the characters: four deciduous species (broad maple, flat-canopy oak, white-barked birch with hanging clumps, columnar poplar) whose crown facets are coloured by normal, three faceted pines, mossy boulders, ribbed and carved pumpkins, houses and barns with emissive windows, haystacks, hay bales, fences, stumps, plus shore reeds with cattails and lily pads as ground decals.
rules: Trees come in designed species, not jittered copies: maple (h 56, one flattened crown + 4 side lobes), oak (h 62, 4-lobe flat canopy + one higher lobe, two branch forks), birch (h 64, white bark #ece6da with dark marks #4a4540, 4 clumps on alternate sides), poplar (h 78, one tall column crown).
Crown colour by facet normal: dark underside, mid body, light sunlit top from the species triad – the crown reads as one lit volume, never as confetti.

Forests grow in groves: a 210-unit noise field picks the dominant species (pines below 0.4, then maple, oak, birch, poplar), 85 % of trees follow it; density rises from 22 % at the forest edge to 54 % inside.
Pines: 4 stacked jittered cones, dark skirt #3f775c -> #4e8d6e -> light top tier #5c9c79, trunk #8c5c3e, heights 58-82.
Boulders: flattened icosphere (sx 1.25, sz 0.72, radius 5-10) in #b4ab9e / #9a9288 with moss #95ad6c on upward faces, ringed by pebbles and tufts.

Pumpkins, houses (walls #f5ecd8, roof #cf6644), barns (walls #bf5540, roof #7d7f96), haystacks, bales, fences and stumps as before: boxes, lathes and double-sided planes scaled 1.25-1.5x, emissive windows #ffd77a.
Tall props fade to alpha 0.42 when the main character is behind them; every prop casts a sun-projected shadow multiplied into the ground at 0.62 in #7d86c4.

effects.name: Core flash
effects.how: A faceted star burst (5-8 points, inner radius 36 %) in a warm or cold rim colour with a white inner star rotated half a point, growing r0 -> r1 with outQuad over 0.12-0.22 s and fading with k^2 – the first layer of every hit, vanish, pickup and celebration.

effects.name: Faceted shards
effects.how: Flat triangles and 4-sided plates (32 %) with gravity 260 and drag 1.6, colour from an 8-step brightness palette of the source chosen by |cos(rotation)| so they flicker like spinning facets; they bounce, land, rest and shrink in the last 35 % of their life. Leaf-green chips and gold emissive chips (with a small additive glow) are mixed in where the source has them.

effects.name: Faceted ground ring
effects.how: A 12-gon on the ground plane (y squash 0.5) expanding r0 -> r1 with outCubic, stroke width lw * (1 - t); larger bursts stagger a second ring by 0.08-0.12 s.

effects.name: Residue patch
effects.how: A flat 7-vertex faceted patch (radius 8-20, jitter 28 %) tinted with the source (#5a4060, #9fb6e8, #4a3a4a) fading in over 0.12 s and out over the last 45 % of 0.9-2 s – what is left where something vanished.

effects.name: Facet break-up
effects.how: A vanishing creature swells (1.16 x / 0.92 y) and whites out for the first 14 % of the sequence, then its hit pose is cut by 9 clip polygons (an inner core of 3 + an outer ring of 6) that fly out and up, spin, land on the ground and fade; spirits drift up and shrink instead, the colossus crumbles heavily. Capped at 6 per frame (the rest sink and fade).

effects.name: Ground-opening appear
effects.how: A dark faceted hole opens (outQuad), 5 cracks run out, 6 soil chunks (#8a6448, #a47a57, #6b4e3c) are pushed up and thrown aside; the creature rises out of the clipped hole with outBack (overshoots, stretches 1.13 on the way up, squashes 0.9 on landing). Spirits materialise: fade in with a 28 Hz flicker, drop 14 units and un-stretch from 1.5 to 1 inside a faceted frost ring.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: A flattened lathe seed (#f8ebc6 / rim #dfc58c) pre-rendered in 8 roll frames, rotated to its direction, with a tapered cream trail triangle (#fff6dc, alpha .45, up to 16 units) and a dark ground dot.

effects.name: Gem and orbiting lantern
effects.how: 8-face octahedron (mint #4fe3b0 r 2.1 / sky #5cbdf6 r 3.1) spinning 8 frames over a quarter turn with a soft halo and an eased bob that holds at top and bottom; every ~2.6 s a 4-point white glint catches the sun. Lanterns are small lilac-and-cream carved meshes hovering 9 ± 1.2 units in an additive warm glow.

atmosphere.summary: Soft afternoon tabletop light: one warm sun from the upper left with a cool-sky / warm-ground ambient, blurred indigo cast shadows falling to the lower right, additive warm glows around emissive parts, and a screen-space tilt-shift with a soft violet side vignette that makes the scene read as a photographed miniature.
rules: Cast shadows: mesh vertices projected along the sun onto the ground, blurred 1.4-2.4 units at alpha 0.5-0.62, plus a radial AO blob (radius 5-30 units, alpha 0.85-0.9), recoloured to #2c3263 for characters (drawn at alpha 0.5, ghosts 0.3) or #7d86c4 for props (multiplied into the ground at 0.62).
Glows are additive radial sprites only: warm rgba(255,214,120,.75) -> rgba(255,140,40,0) (r 24), small rgba(255,225,140,.9) -> rgba(255,150,50,0) (r 10), cold rgba(220,240,255,.5) (r 12).

Tilt-shift: the top 20 % and bottom 17 % of the frame are copied into 1/8-size canvases, tinted with a light haze rgba(232,238,250,.34 -> 0) on top and violet rgba(70,62,110,0 -> .26) at the bottom, and drawn back in 7 slices with alpha (1 - e)^1.6.
Side vignette: 9 %-wide gradients rgba(60,55,100,.22) -> 0 on the left and right.
Modal overlay: radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 46%, rgba(255,246,232,.30), rgba(66,56,104,.66)) with a 3 px backdrop blur.
No bloom and no colour grading beyond tilt-shift and vignette; shadows and vignettes are always indigo/violet, never black or grey.

Ambient motion, always slower than the actors: leaves in the grove colours tumble down over the woods (one per other 64-unit cell, 5-8 s fall, flip with cos(3.4 t)), and faceted glints blink slowly on pond facets.

ui.summary: Soft, rounded, toy-like HUD: cream pill panels (#fffaf2) with a violet drop shadow and a subtle inset bottom lip, thick cream borders around pill bars with glossy gradient fills and a white highlight stripe, round icon badges overlapping the start of bars, and cards with a 28 px radius that lift 8 px on hover. Text in Baloo 2 800, ink #3e3a58. Icons are the same low-poly meshes rendered into round radial-gradient badges.

motion: Main character walk: 8 rig poses per stride (frame = floor(anim * 0.5 * 8) % 8); legs swing ±0.58 rad with the knee folding up to 1.15 rad in the swing phase, arms counter-swing ±0.62 rad with elbows bending forward, torso leans 0.11, twists ±0.12 and rolls over the stance leg; cape hem, scarf tail and head leaf peak about 1.3 rad after the bob (follow-through).
Idle: 4 breathing poses over 2 s (chest +0.14, arms out, head lagging the chest), a blink pose for 0.14 s every 3.6 s (eyes become slits, face glow drops to 40 %).

Dash: crouch pose for the first 45 ms (anticipation: knees fold, body drops 1.2, arms back), then the airborne lunge (lean 0.42, cape 5 units back and lifted 3.4, scarf streaming) with two cool after-images 7 units apart and three cream speed facets.
Hurt: hurt pose while hurtT > 0.62 (~130 ms: thrown back, arms up, squeezed eyes, open mouth), tilted away 0.16 rad with a white flash; then blink at 18 Hz during invulnerability.

Creatures: 6 walk poses + hit pose. Small creature waddles (roll ±0.13, squash 0.935 at contact / stretch 1.065 at passing, body up 1.1 at passing, leaves lag 1.3 rad); colossus drops 1.5 units on every footfall; spirit hovers with an eased triangle wave (holds at the extremes, 2.2 s period, own phase per actor) and swims with alternating mitten strokes. Per-actor phase comes from anim / seed, so crowds never move in lock-step.

Hit reaction (~140 ms, driven by flash 1 -> 0): hit pose + white flash while flash > 0.25, sprite rotated up to 0.26 rad in the push direction, squash 1.09 / 0.92, pushed 1.5 units; colossus tilts only 0.12.

Facing is a smoothed yaw (angleLerp: 0.22 main character, 0.5 while dashing, 0.16 small creatures, 0.08 colossus) quantised to 16 baked angles; without velocity, actors turn to a 3/4 view of their facing side.
Gems spin 1.5 quarter-turns per second; lanterns hover at 4 rad/s; floating numbers pop 0.55 -> 1.15 scale in the first 14 % of their life.
do: Build every visible thing as a real triangle mesh and flat-shade it with the same sun vector and ambient constants.
Rig characters from separate part meshes on pivots and bake each pose at 16 yaws; derive the hip height from the stance leg.
Give every action its sequence: crouch before the lunge, hit pose before the flash fades, swell before the break-up, a ground opening before the rise.
Colour crowns and tiers by face normal (dark / mid / light) and let the sun do the rest; keep facets large (5-9 segment lathes, icospheres sub 0-1).
Compose the ground: groves of one species, litter under crowns in their own colours, reeds on shores, flowers in patches, pebbles along paths.
Ground every object with a sun-projected, blurred indigo shadow plus an AO blob.
Finish with the tilt-shift bands (top 20 % hazy-light, bottom 17 % violet) and a soft side vignette.
dont: Don't add black outlines or cel ink – the look depends on outline-free facets.
Don't use smooth gradients or Gouraud/Phong shading on models; one colour per triangle.
Don't pick facet colours at random per face – random tones read as confetti; pick by normal (models) or by a low-frequency noise field (ground).
Don't scatter decals evenly over a biome; place them where something causes them (a crown above, a shore, an edge, a path).
Don't render meshes live every frame for crowds – bake poses and blit sprites.
Don't fake animation by squashing sprites; squash only accents a real pose (contact, landing, hit).
Don't make shadows grey or black, and don't mix camera pitches or light directions between assets.
performance: All meshes are baked once at init: 16 yaws x 16 main-character poses, 16 x 7 per creature set (two small-creature variants), props, decals and icons, plus the white flash tints of the hit/hurt/lunge poses (pre-baked so no canvas is created during play). Per frame only drawImage blits, a few transforms (hit tilt, spawn rise), additive glows and particles are drawn. Break-ups clip 9 pieces per creature and are capped at 6 per frame. Ground chunks (256 units) are built incrementally with a generator; litter, decals and prop shadows are baked into them. Ambient leaves use a memoised per-cell lookup. The tilt-shift costs two 1/8-scale band copies per frame and is the largest per-frame cost.
